ruleset.name: Unused formal parameters
ruleset.description:
Second PHPMD leg: UnusedFormalParameter only.
This rule lives in its own ruleset because PHPMD honours <exclude-pattern> ONLY as a direct child of <ruleset>; nested inside a <rule> it is parsed and discarded (ConductionNL/.github#155). A direct child, however, is applied by PDepend at file-collection time and drops the file from EVERY rule in the ruleset. Isolating UnusedFormalParameter here means the lib/BackgroundJob exclusion applies to this rule and this rule ALONE - every other rule still analyses lib/BackgroundJob in the main leg.
Why lib/BackgroundJob is excluded from THIS rule: OCP\BackgroundJob\TimedJob (and QueuedJob) declare `abstract protected function run($argument)`. A job that needs no argument still cannot drop the parameter - PHP would reject the narrower signature. The signature cannot change.
This replaces three opaque phpmd.baseline.xml entries (CallbackOverdueJob, EmailSyncJob, TaskEscalationJob) with one scoped, documented exclusion that states its own reason.
The pattern is */lib/BackgroundJob/* and deliberately NOT */BackgroundJob/*. The broader form also excludes any ordinary class that merely sits under a path segment of that name - e.g. lib/Service/BackgroundJob/ - which has no mandated signature and must stay analysed. Measured with a positive control (PHPMD 2.15, PHP 8.4, absolute paths): with */lib/X/* a probe in lib/Service/X/ IS reported, while with */X/* it is silently swallowed. Both forms correctly exclude the app's own lib/BackgroundJob/. This matches the fleet-canonical */lib/Migration/* shape used in nextcloud-app-template #125, doriath #157, larpingapp #263 and planix #315.
